thread:
incident-bot: PAGING: KV cache memory spike detected on continuous-batching ring in eu-west-1. shard-group=12 cache_mem=87% - severity: high. Paging on-call.

sam: ack — i'm on it. seeing p95 latency bump and GC churn. grabbing heap snapshots.

maya: i noticed a config roll around 23:12 UTC that increased `max_batch_bytes` from 1MB -> 2.5MB for batch-optimizer v2. could explain larger KV entries and cache blowup.

eli: @infra-eng can you confirm any kernel/runtime changes? also observing increased KV page handoffs in logs.

dina: quick customer-impact check: AcmeCorp shows elevated 5xx and tail latency (high), BetaApps has increased retries (medium). Others show slight latency noise. no data loss reported.

sam: mitigation proposal: flip emergency flag `batching.safe_mode` to limit continuous batching window & fall back for long contexts, and apply per-customer overrides to the worst-off customers. need approval to proceed.

maya: SRE +1. suggest canary first: route 10% of traffic to safe_mode, monitor KV mem and tail latency for 15m.

sam: executing canary now.

Deploy-bot: [feature-flag] request by sam: set batching.safe_mode=on (rollout=canary:10%). applying to blue-canary ring.

maya: watching metrics — canary nodes show cache_mem down ~35% in 4m, p95 trending down ~70ms. promising.

eli: applying per-customer override for acme-001 to disable continuous_batching while we stabilize. command: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/overrides \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
 -d '{"customer_id":"acme-001","feature":"continuous_batching","state":"off","ttl":"2h","reason":"active_kv_memory_surge"}'
```

Deploy-bot: override applied → acme-001 continuous_batching=off (actor=eli).

AcmePM-bot: Notified Acme primary contact: "We've made a temporary config change to mitigate instability. Expect improved latency; we'll follow up with a postmortem." Ack received.

sam: 12m post-canary snapshot: canary nodes global avg cache_mem fell from 88% -> 63%. global p95 reduced 220ms -> 145ms. Acme errors back to baseline after override.

dina: customer-impact note for handoff: affected: AcmeCorp (high), BetaApps (medium). region: eu-west-1. mitigations: canary safe_mode + per-customer overrides. no data corruption. next steps: widen canary to 40% in 10m if stable; open PR to reduce default max_batch_bytes and add KV growth alert.

maya: opening PR with config diff: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/5123 — lowering max_batch_bytes default to 1.2MB and adding `kv_cache_growth_rate` alert rule. link added to incident doc.

sam: recommend widening safe_mode from 10% -> 40% now. rollback criteria: errors >2x baseline or p95 >2x. frank will take handoff in 20m; i'll remain incident lead.

frank: taking next oncall. i'll continue rollout, monitor, and run heapdump if any node >90% mem. ping me in DMs for urgent items.

matt-healthbot: health checks configured: heartbeat every 2m, alert on cache_mem delta >10% over 5m window.

sam: leaving runbook notes in incident ticket: 1) if mem spikes after widening, revert to 10% and apply more per-customer overrides; 2) collect heap dumps for nodes >90% and attach to ticket; 3) follow-up: QoS for KV eviction and reduce default batch size.

frank: handoff snapshot: safe_mode at 40%, acme override active, eu-west-1 cache_mem stable ~60-66%, p95 ~150ms. continuing monitoring.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated (monitoring). Postmortem ticket PMT-2026-112 created in #postmortems.

frank: closing thread for now, will reopen if alerts re-fire. :thumbsup:
